subject: Priority assignation for committed and opportunistic Dedicated SKU - CloudLoom / Zenith coordination
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudloom.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Jon Perez <jon.perez@zenith-ai.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask & timing for CL-1279

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — CloudLoom wants to move from pilot to a production Dedicated deployment. High level ask: 40 A100-equivalent GPUs across us-west/us-east (initial release) starting around Sep 15. We expect steady inference volume and are prepared to sign a 12-month reserved SKU if we can lock a start window and a predictable capex/commit.

Two quick constraints from our side: 1) SOC2 evidence required before cutover, and 2) procurement needs a term sheet by Sep 1 to complete Q3 budget.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can hold a hard reservation or at least a soft-reserve (guaranteed baseline + burst) while we finalize signature? If not, what prioritization rubric would determine our placement relative to other committed deals?

Attaching a draft term sheet for context (SOW and expected timeline).

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Partnerships, CloudLoom
Attachment: CL-1279-term-sheet.pdf

---

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@cloudloom.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask & timing for CL-1279

Samira — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We're supportive of CloudLoom moving to Dedicated; the main blocker is fleet planning for mid-September. I've looped in Karthik and Marcus from Capacity/Deals so we can map a concrete allocation and propose options (guaranteed vs opportunistic burst).

Karthik/Marcus — can you run a quick delta vs planned Q3 capacity and confirm whether we can make a hard reservation for 40 A100-equivalents starting Sep 15, or whether we should propose a stepped plan (20 guaranteed + 20 burst)? Please include trade-offs for existing committed customers (impacted deals), and an initial recommendation by EOD.

Samira — we'll aim to get a term-sheet-friendly proposal to you by tomorrow so procurement can proceed.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:27:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask & timing for CL-1279

Lauren — quick inventory and recommendation after a run with infra:

Summary of fleet availability (as of 25 Aug):
- Free pool (usable for Dedicated reservations before Sep 15): ~56 A100-equivalent GPUs across two US regions (us-west, us-east).
- Committed carries (already reserved by contracts starting Sep/Oct): ~34 A100-equivalents.

CloudLoom ask: 40 GPUs starting Sep 15. That exceeds safe guaranteed capacity. Two feasible options: 
1) Conservative guaranteed: guarantee 20 GPUs from Sep 15 and commit to burstable access to an additional 20 GPUs subject to short-notice capacity, with SLAs that reflect burst best-effort. This keeps our reserved commitments intact and preserves room for a new high-priority enterprise if they sign.
2) Aggressive re-prioritization: reassign 24 GPUs from lower-ARR opportunistic reservations for a guaranteed 40. This would require contract-level exceptions for at least two customers (IDs: ZN-334 and SUP-812) and an exec sign-off due to SLA impacts.

Trade-offs: option 1 reduces risk of churn among already-signed customers; option 2 meets CloudLoom's ask fully but increases legal/procurement friction (they'd need credits/compensation).

Recommendation: propose option 1 to CloudLoom immediately (20 guarantee + 20 burst) with a path to move to full guarantee if DocuSign is returned and the legal term-sheet includes an expedited compensation clause for any displaced customers. See attached capacity_plan_Q3_v3.xlsx for the region-by-region breakdown and timing.

I'll also sketch a priority matrix to justify escalation if legal/exec want to push CloudLoom ahead of other deals.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Capacity Planning & Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_plan_Q3_v3.xlsx

On Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:05:22 -0700, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai wrote:
> Samira — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We're supportive of CloudLoom moving to Dedicated; the main blocker is fleet planning for mid-September. I've looped in Karthik and Marcus from Capacity/Deals so we can map a concrete allocation and propose options (guaranteed vs opportunistic burst).

---

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:50:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask & timing for CL-1279

Folks — adding a prioritization rubric and recommended operational steps. Draft rubric (weighting):
- Contracted ARR (first 30%): committed revenue on signed contract (highest weight).
- Signed start date and onboarding dependencies (20%): earlier start windows increase weight.
- Security/compliance lead time (15%): SOC2 + other audits create non-trivial lead time.
- Strategic partnership / go-to-market obligations (15%).
- Churn risk / customer health (10%).
- Penalty/credit exposure (10%).

Applying this to current near-term deals: CloudLoom scores high on ARR and compliance lead time; Zenith (ZN-334) is mid-ARR but already signed and on a tighter SLA. Given the weights, CloudLoom would rank slightly above a few opportunistic trials, but below fully-signed contracts with high SLA exposure.

Operational steps I propose now:
1) Offer CloudLoom 20 guaranteed + 20 burst (consistent with Karthik).
2) Draft a short-term compensation clause (credit for preemption) and insert into the term-sheet if CloudLoom signs within 72 hours.
3) Create a temporary "soft-reserve" in the scheduler: tag the requested GPUs to CloudLoom with preemption policy.
4) If CloudLoom returns DocuSign and pays a deposit, convert burst -> guaranteed and notify impacted customers with 7-day remediation/credit offer.

I'll flag this to Vivek as an exception request; we should avoid making this the default policy but allow it for high-fit enterprise deals. Attached: priority_matrix.csv sample.

Marcus Lin
Principal, Customer Success Strategy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: priority_matrix.csv

---

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask & timing for CL-1279

Thanks team — I agree with the conservative path (20 guaranteed + 20 burst) as a temporary exception, with the explicit caveat that we tie the conversion to a signed contract + deposit and a compensation clause for preemption. Action items: 

- Legal to draft the short compensation clause and confirm enforceability (Neha) — due EOD Thu.
- Lauren to share the updated term-sheet and the DocuSign link with Samira (send 1-hour SLA for signature once we issue).
- Karthik to open JIRA CAP-4459 to create the soft-reserve flag and preemption enforcement rules (assign to infra/allocator).
- Marcus to prepare a customer communication template for impacted customers (credit + notice).

If any of these items fail (legal says no, infra can't implement preemption flag in time), we will fallback to only 20 guaranteed and no burst. Please update this thread when items are done.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Production
Redwood Inference

DocuSign link pending: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/contracts/DocuSignLink-CL1279
